verdict.rationale: Skyvern publishes its source in a public GitHub repository (Skyvern-AI/skyvern). Its own llms.txt describes it as open-source, and a community user confirms the code is AGPL3-licensed. Docs for self-hosting the server via pip, Docker Compose or Kubernetes support that the runnable code is available. Missing for 10: first-party statement of the license terms (the AGPL3 identification comes only from a community comment), and clarity on whether cloud-only features (e.g. CAPTCHA solving, proxies, Copilot) are in the open repo.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Skyvern is an open-source, AI-powered browser automation platform.
a no-code workflow builder to help both technical and non-technical users automate manual workflows on any website
Run the Skyvern server on your own machine or cluster with pip, Docker Compose, or Kubernetes
